title: Prior ozone and warmth gave no repeated rise in annual bird richness change magnitude in four US samples in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether prior ozone and warmth were linked to larger absolute annual changes in recorded bird richness. We used 22,384 consecutive same-observer survey pairs from a published US panel. Four tests used eastern and western regions in 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. Models controlled route-observer and state-year differences, weather and survey conditions at both visits. The two eastern interaction intervals included zero. The western estimates were positive in the early period and negative in the later period. Both western intervals included zero with monitors within 25 km. Year and two-way clustering also made the later western interval cross zero. Thus, a repeated rise was not established. This outcome measures change magnitude, not ecological variance or taxon replacement. Shared source records, coarse exposures, small cluster counts, monitor selection and detection error limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and reproduction instructions. Source record tables remain external.

display.caption: The ozone by warmth slope for absolute annual recorded-richness change. Bars are 98.75 percent state-cluster intervals. Regions use separate records. Time periods can share routes. A common positive association did not repeat.
